## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

2 November 2001

## Circular to Brokers

## Caution! Two More Brokers Defrauded Despite SFC Warning.

Two more brokers have suffered financial losses as a result of suspected fraudulent activities by  walk-in  clients.  It  appears  that  the  scam  was  carried  out  by  the  same  walk-in client responsible for a similar fraud on other intermediaries a few months ago.

## Beware of fraudulent activities

The  SFC  issued  a  circular  on  16  August  2001  warning  intermediaries  against  fraudulent activities by walk-in clients and outlining their usual practice:

- walk-in clients opened securities accounts with the intermediaries and shortly after the accounts were opened, placed orders to buy shares in a listed company;
- when required by the intermediaries to deposit the funds for the  purchases, the walk-in clients  would  produce  pay-in  slips  which  showed  funds  had  been  deposited  into  the intermediaries' bank accounts by cheques;
- after  the  purchases  were  concluded,  the  intermediaries  were    advised  by  their  bankers (usually immediately after the market close) that the cheques deposited by the walk-in clients had bounced at which time it was found that  these cheques were issued by third parties;
- the walk-in clients, however, could not be located as the  personal information provided by them to the intermediaries was fake.

The circular also advised intermediaries to  exercise caution in dealing with new clients and put in place satisfactory internal control procedures to protect their operations accordingly.

## Take Precaution

Losses could h ave been avoided in the latest cases had the defrauded brokers carried out the preventive  measures  suggested  in  the  circular.    Brokers  should  observe  the  'Know  Your Clients' rule and when dealing with new clients, it is in the interest of the brokers to ensure that they have cleared funds to satisfy orders.
